about.title: Upland Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product doesn't announce itself. In Upland, it might be a space heater that catches fire in a home off Euclid Avenue, a tire that separates on SR-210, or a children's toy with a piece that never should have come loose. When something you bought and used as intended ends up hurting you, California law treats the case differently than an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict liability, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that particular unit was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. That opens the door to claims against everyone in the chain of sale: the maker, the distributor, and the store where it was purchased. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Upland residents in San Bernardino County with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency. Hold on to the product. It is the heart of your case.

whyChoose.title: Why Upland Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: You typically don't need to prove the company was negligent — only that the product was defective and the defect caused your injury. The attorney we connect you with can evaluate whether your case fits a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.title: The Product Is Evidence
items.desc: A defective item that gets thrown away or repaired can weaken a claim before it starts. Attorneys in our network know how to preserve, document, and test the product so its condition speaks for itself.

items.title: More Than One Party May Answer
items.desc: In California, the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer can all be held responsible for a defective product. Identifying every link in that chain matters, and an independent attorney handles it on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My airbag didn't deploy in a crash on Foothill Boulevard in Upland. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Upland recorded 430 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a vehicle component that did not perform as designed. A claim against the other driver and a separate product claim against the airbag or vehicle manufacturer can proceed together. Don't let the vehicle be scrapped or the airbag module removed until an attorney has looked at it.

items.question: I already threw the broken product away. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, though it is harder. Photos, receipts, packaging, the model number, and any recall notices can help reconstruct what failed. An attorney can also look for the same defect in other units of the same product. Reach out sooner rather than later so whatever evidence remains can be secured.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney in San Bernardino County?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we are not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles product liability claims on a contingency basis, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. There is no obligation to hire anyone after the conversation.
